literal: Having thrown the hand-spear at the elephant, he who returns, plucking out the body-spear, smiles.
translation: He who returns after hurling his hand-spear at an elephant smiles with joy as he plucks out another spear lodged in his own body.
modern: தன் கையில் இருந்த வேலை யானையின் மீது எறிந்துவிட்டுத் திரும்புகிறவன், தன் உடம்பில் பாய்ந்திருக்கும் வேலைப் பிடுங்கி மகிழ்ந்து சிரிப்பான்.
explanation: This couplet illustrates the fierce pride and valor of a classical warrior. Having thrown his only spear to fell a war-elephant, he walks back weaponless. When he realizes an enemy's spear is lodged deep in his own chest or body, he does not lament his wound; instead, he smiles with joy because he has found a new weapon to fight with. The word 'பறியா' shows his eagerness as he plucks the weapon from his own flesh, and 'நகும்' captures his triumphant smile at this discovery.
